title: Customer escalation matrix for offline private upgrades + hosted fallbacks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: A set of enterprise customers running Redwood Private (air-gapped / offline upgrades) have reported regressions during recent model rollouts. Symptoms: elevated hallucination rates and increased token latency in private planes vs hosted baseline, canary slices failing validation, and sticky KV-cache divergence after rollback. This ticket defines an operational escalation matrix, triage playbook, and a coordinated fix/communication flow that covers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment topologies.

Problem context: Private upgrade workflows differ from hosted - nodes are upgraded offline via signed artifacts, and network-limited customers cannot immediately fallback to hosted variants. During the last rollout we observed a model kernel selection mismatch (quantized vs non-quantized path) introduced by a packaging change that only manifested on private appliances with older CUDA drivers. Canary traffic flagged quality regressions but the rollback left per-tenant KV caches in a stale state, causing repeated degradations on subsequent rollouts. Dedicated customers experienced transient increased latency when autoscaling attempted to repopulate caches.

Goals: 1) Produce a clear escalation matrix (severity -> owner -> initial actions -> time-to-first-response). 2) Define an offline-safe live-fix path (signed hotpatch artifact + safe-module-replace procedure) and an authoritative rollback procedure that includes KV cache reconciliation. 3) Provide templated customer communications and SLA commitments for high-impact escalations. 4) Integrate observability checks into pre-rollout gating for private images (driver/torch/kernel checks + synthetic story-based evals).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the full automated rollback broker; it focuses on the human-run escalation matrix, runbook updates, and a repeatable manual patch procedure for offline private upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: A documented escalation matrix exists and is reviewed by SRE, Field Engineering, and Customer Success
A tested manual hotpatch workflow for offline private appliances is documented (steps + safety checks + signed artifact verification)
Rollback procedure includes KV cache drain/reconcile steps and has a small dry-run executed on a staging private node
Pre-rollout checklist extended: driver/kernel compatibility checks + story-based synthetic evals added to CI gating for private images
Customer communication templates (initial triage, follow-up, post-mortem) added to shared drive and verified with legal/comms
